wrongs.claim: The Admin Overview hub has exactly 21 cards in 5 sections: Lead Distribution (3), Follow Up (4), Account (8), Integrations (2), Customize (4)
wrongs.correct: 21 cards in 5 sections: Lead Distribution (3), Follow Up (4), Account (6), Integrations (4), Customize (4)
wrongs.evidence: shot-33_full.png and all four quadrant images show the Admin Overview hub with 21 cards across 5 sections, but the per-section breakdown differs from the claim. Account section contains exactly 6 cards (Business Registration, Team, Import, Phone Numbers, Company, Email Domain Authentication) — not 8. Integrations section contains exactly 4 cards (API Keys & Lead Email, Pixel, IDX Integrations, All Integrations) — not 2. Lead Distribution (3), Follow Up (4), and Customize (4) are correct. Actual distribution: Lead Distribution(3) + Follow Up(4) + Account(6) + Integrations(4) + Customize(4) = 21.

wrongs.claim: Phone row SMS action button is a 40 pt circle with background color #7b7ec8 (purple); Call action button is a 40 pt circle with background color #3dc896 (green)
wrongs.evidence:
Pixel sampling of mob-02_t.png (the top band showing the phone row clearly at high resolution) reveals:

SMS (message) button dominant fill color: #7595e8 — a bright blue-lavender (R=117, G=149, B=232), confirmed across 4,370 pixels in the button zone. The spec claims #7b7ec8 (R=123, G=126, B=200), a more muted, red-leaning purple. The green channel diverges by 23 units and the blue channel by 32 units — a clearly different hue.

Call button dominant fill color: #4ad09f — a teal-green/mint (R=74, G=208, B=159), confirmed solid across the entire 5×5 center sample. The spec claims #3dc896 (R=61, G=200, B=150) — the same teal-green family but measurably lighter and more saturated in the actual screenshot (R off by 13, G off by 8, B off by 9).

Both circles are present and do appear to be ~40pt in diameter, and the hues (purple-ish for SMS, green for Call) are directionally correct — but both specific hex values are wrong.

wrongs.claim: Max automated emails per contact per day: 4 (hard platform limit regardless of how many action plans are enrolled simultaneously; excess queued to next day)
wrongs.correct: Max automated emails per contact per day: 4 (hard platform limit). Excess emails FAIL TO SEND permanently — they are not queued to the next day. Error returned: "This person has already received the maximum amount of automated emails today."
wrongs.evidence: The FUB help article "Why did my action plan email fail to send?" (help.followupboss.com/hc/en-us/articles/4402377886743) confirms the 4-email-per-contact-per-day hard limit is real, but directly contradicts what happens to excess emails. The page states verbatim: "If a person receives more than 4 emails sent by action plans in one day, those emails will fail to send with the following message: 'This person has already received the maximum amount of automated emails today.'" Excess emails are DROPPED (fail to send), not queued to the next day. There is no automatic retry or queue-to-tomorrow behavior described anywhere in the documentation.

wrongs.claim: Webhook limit: 2 webhooks per event type per account; webhook endpoint must respond within 10 seconds with a 2XX status; retry schedule on failure: 1 min → 5 min → 5 min → 10 min → 30 min; webhooks auto-disabled after >50% failure over 48 hours that do not recover within 1 week
wrongs.correct: 2 webhooks per event per system (registered API integration), not per account. A single FUB account with multiple registered systems can have more than 2 webhooks per event type in total (2 per system × N systems).
wrongs.evidence: The FUB webhooks-guide page (docs.followupboss.com/reference/webhooks-guide) states verbatim: "There is a limit of two web hooks per event per system which can be registered." The word "system" refers to a registered API integration/client, not the FUB account as a whole. Multiple integrations on the same account can each register up to 2 webhooks per event type independently. The spec says "per account," which would incorrectly imply a hard global cap of 2 per event type across all integrations on the account. The remaining sub-claims are all exactly confirmed: 10-second response timeout with 2XX status, retry schedule 1 min → 5 min → 5 min → 10 min → 30 min, and auto-disable after >50% failure over 48 hours if not recovered within 1 week.

wrongs.claim: Grow plan per-seat annual price: $828/yr per user (observed live on Ryan Realty account); Calling add-on on Grow plan: $39/user/month per enabled user; Calling add-on free trial: 14 days, up to 20 users per account, available once every 6 months
wrongs.correct: Grow plan annual billing price: $58/month billed annually = $696/yr per user. The $828/yr figure is the monthly billing rate ($69/mo) annualized — not the annual plan rate. Calling add-on on monthly billing: $39/user/month; on annual billing: $33/user/month. Trial terms are correct: 14 days, up to 20 users, once every 6 months.
wrongs.evidence: The followupboss.com/pricing page shows the Grow plan at $69/month (monthly billing) or $58/month billed annually. The "annual price" (annual billing plan) is $58 × 12 = $696/yr per user — NOT $828/yr. The $828/yr figure equals $69 × 12 (monthly rate annualized), which is what Ryan Realty would pay per year if on a monthly billing plan, not the annual plan price. The calling add-on at $39/user/month is confirmed for monthly billing (annual billing rate is $33/user/month per the pricing page). The trial terms are fully verified: 14 days, up to 20 users per account, available once every 6 months (confirmed verbatim by the FUB help article "How can I try the FUB Calling for free?").

wrongs.claim: `crm-gmail-sync` cron runs every 15 minutes and handles two-way email sync for matt@, rebeccapeterson@, and paul@ryan-realty.com
wrongs.correct: The cron is one-way ingest (Gmail → CRM timeline). Two-way email capability (send from CRM) is provided by `sendCrmEmail()` in lib/crm/gmail.ts, invoked from a separate endpoint, not this cron.
wrongs.evidence: The route at app/api/cron/crm-gmail-sync/route.ts is one-way ingest only, not two-way. Its GET handler calls only `syncMailboxWindow`, which uses `getGmailFor(mailboxEmail, READONLY)` — read-only Gmail scope — and the route header explicitly says "pulls all three broker mailboxes into the unified timeline." The vercel.json schedule `"9,24,39,54 * * * *"` (every 15 minutes) and the three mailboxes (matt@ryan-realty.com, rebeccapeterson@ryan-realty.com, paul@ryan-realty.com via CRM_MAILBOXES) are both correct. Only the "two-way" characterization is wrong: outbound send (`sendCrmEmail()`) exists in lib/crm/gmail.ts but is a separate function invoked from a different route, not by this cron.
